reason: The essay clears the non-obviousness bar: its load-bearing move is not 'injection exists' but the structural reframe that MCP standardizes a known-dangerous pattern by placing the trust boundary at a client architected to forward, not to check, so the exposure is replicated across every conforming client rather than being one team's bug. The angle is sound and self-aware. The 'This is just prompt injection' section is the piece's spine: it steelmans the strongest objection (unfalsifiable-padding charge, contingent-fact charge) and answers it with a checkable structural claim (where the boundary sits, who defends it, what the SDK ships), even conceding a falsification condition. The browser/untrusted-page analogy is apt and recurs with discipline. Structure earns the length: boundary-moved -> concrete mechanism (model-visible/UI-hidden gap) -> objection -> client-side fix (three ranked, concrete mitigations), each section doing distinct work with no padding. The so-what lands with actionable teeth (static metadata analysis, decision-path tracking, runtime display) and correctly derives 'no server patch to wait for' from the thesis. Prose is tight and declarative. Worth publishing as a considered essay.
